episodes.192260: A weak mid-level trough moved across a marginally unstable airmass across northern NY during the late afternoon and evening hours of July 24th. Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon and continued into the evening hours with just a few isolated pulse-type storms that produced severe, damaging winds.
episodes.192313: Scattered thunderstorms moved across northern Illinois during the afternoon and early evening of July 23rd producing isolated wind damage and isolated flooding.
episodes.192314: Scattered thunderstorms moved across southern Lake Michigan during the afternoon and early evening of July 23rd.
episodes.192411: A complex of thunderstorms along a weak and slowly-passing cold front, tracked from northern Illinois into northern central Indiana by midday hours.  Ahead of the boundary, marginally warm yet rather humid surface conditions promoted slow strengthening of a few cells.  A rogue, stronger storm coupled with a layer of dry air aloft to produce severe downdraft winds in rural central Hamilton County.
episodes.192582: Numerous thunderstorms impacted southeast Arizona on July 24, most notably in the Tucson and Safford areas that recorded severe threshold wind gusts.
episodes.192694: A stalled frontal boundary across the Mid Atlantic helped to spark an isolated severe thunderstorm. Winds from this thunderstorm blew down two trees in Halifax County. The storm also produced a funnel cloud.
episodes.192697: A stalled frontal boundary helped to produce scattered thunderstorms that became severe. Winds from these storms blew down a notable number of trees. One of the storms also produced an EF-1 tornado in Halifax County with peak winds at 100 mph, which downed numerous trees and caused structural damage.
episodes.192802: Thunderstorms brought locally heavy rain and a flash flood potential along with strong outflow gusts through Wednesday. Abundant moisture and instability were present as noted by the 0.81 PWAT reading from the 23 July 1200Z KREV sounding this morning. Sufficient clearing also helped temperatures to climb well above average for late July. Short term high-resolution HREF guidance showed an uptick in PWATs Wednesday as deeper moisture expanded northward across western NV and far northeast CA |as a ridge axis slid east with upper level southerly flow increasing ahead of a trough advancing into the Pacific Northwest. A few severe storms with gusts to 60 mph and nickel sized hail were forecasted on 23 July. But flash flooding would be the bigger concern as storms moved either slower or anchored near steep terrain and burn scars. For 24 July, mid level S/SW winds increased which increased both storm motions and shear for storm organization. SPC introduced a marginal risk for severe wind gusts near the Oregon border with similar severe weather threats for stronger outflows and blowing dust reaching the Basin and Range. While storms were expected to move faster, training storm  cells would continue to bring a heightened threat for flash flooding for areas south of I-80 with focus on the eastern Sierra into southern Lyon and Mineral counties. For 25 July, drier and more stable air confined storms to the Basin and Range where activity was forecast to be isolated but still able to produce gusty outflows and areas of blowing dust.

episodes.192866: A few strong storms moved over the Little Rocky Mountains, with one storm producing a severe wind gust.
episodes.192960: A frontal boundary supported scattered thunderstorms across Central New York. Ahead of the front, an unstable environment supported a few severe thunderstorms. Damaging wind gusts were the main hazard. There were multiple reports of trees and wires down across the region.
episodes.192961: A frontal boundary supported scattered thunderstorms in Northeastern Pennsylvania. Ahead of the front, an unstable environment supported one severe thunderstorm. There were just a couple of reports of trees down in Wayne County.
episodes.193022: Scattered thunderstorms developed during the afternoon hours in a warm and unstable airmass.
episodes.193248: Prevailing SSE steering flow focused the daytime sea breeze and boundary collisions across interior NE FL between the I-75 and Highway 301 corridors. Locally gusty winds and heavy, flooding rainfall occurred.
episodes.193404: A stalled frontal boundary across Virginia remained in place through the day and night. South of this boundary, isolated to scattered storms developed in the afternoon and evening. A stronger batch of storms developed in the evening and overnight, producing damaging wind reports across Orange, Durham, and Franklin Counties of central North Carolina. Storms continued into the 24th of July across the Coastal Plain.
episodes.193405: A stalled frontal boundary across Virginia remained in place early in the morning on the 24th of July. Storms from earlier in the mid to late evening hours of the 23rd continued into the overnight hours and into the morning of the 24th of July. These lingering storms produced isolated flash flooding across Scotland County.
episodes.193475: Classic summertime pattern favored the development of strong storms, with one such storm becoming severe. This caused a downburst and resulted in wind damage in Richland County. Strong moisture convergence and high precipitable water several hours later caused training thunderstorms over downtown Columbia leading to flash flooding.
episodes.193484: A stalled boundary across central South Carolina, combined with extremely high precipitable water values lead to a series of training thunderstorms and flash flooding. Skinny instability and unidirectional flow aloft caused the line of storms to move parallel to the boundary with widespread 2-3 inch per hour rates for several hours in the central Midlands. Saturated soils and some sub-severe gusty outflow winds knocked several trees down in Newberry county.
episodes.194002: Scattered showers and thunderstorms impacted eastern New York on July 24, 2024 as a result of the passing of an upper-level disturbance. A couple of thunderstorms became severe in nature, producing severe wind gusts that contributed to several reports of tree and wire damage in the Eastern Catskills and Upper-Hudson Valley. An isolated, weak EF0 tornado was also reported near Broadalbin which also resulted in tree damage on both commercial and personal property. Locally heavy downpours lead to an isolated report of minor flooding in the Lake George area.
episodes.194008: Scattered thunderstorms produced wind gusts in excess of 34 knots along the coast and a waterspout just offshore of Panama City Beach during the July 21-24 time period.
episodes.194297: An environment characterized by strong synoptic support for lift, up to 2000 J/kg of surface-based CAPE, and good synoptic support for lift fostered the development of a few broken lines of thunderstorms during the afternoon of July 24th.  The strongest were mostly north of Interstate 80, creating several instances of downed trees.
episodes.194511: A shortwave trough brought a cold front through southeast Oregon. This cold front brought a significant shift in the dry and hot weather with high based thunderstorms and associated winds. Strong winds, especially in Baker County, brought minor damage to several small cities.
episodes.194512: A shortwave trough brought a cold front through southwest Idaho. This cold front brought a significant shift in the dry and hot weather with high based thunderstorms and associated winds.
episodes.194532: With the subtropical high pressure situated over southern Nevada, the steering flow was from the northeast. Thunderstorm activity developed over the Mogollon Rim during the early afternoon hours and was steered southwestward towards Yavapai, northwestern Maricopa, and La Paz Counties. The overall environment was characterized by MLCAPE values of 500-1000 J/KG, with DCAPE values near 2000 J/KG. Thus, conditions were favorable for strong to severe downburst wind gusts to materialize with any thunderstorm activity that developed.
episodes.194561: A pre-frontal trough and cold front crossing western and north central New York caused a few rounds of thunderstorms through the day on July 24, 2024. The strongest storms, reaching severe criteria, occurred with the trough as it tracked east with increased instability and shear ahead of it. While most of the thunderstorms remained below severe criteria, a few damage reports were received, including a tornado.
episodes.194564: A pre-frontal trough and cold front crossing western and north central New York caused a few rounds of thunderstorms through the day on July 24, 2024. The strongest storms, occurred with the trough as it tracked east with increased instability and shear ahead of it.
episodes.194567: A pre-frontal trough and cold front crossing western and north central New York caused a few rounds of thunderstorms through the day on July 24, 2024. The strongest storms, occurred with the trough as it tracked east with increased instability and shear ahead of it.
episodes.194575: Isolated thunderstorms developed across Riverside County during the afternoon hours on the 24th. A severe thunderstorm developed near Desert Center, with strong downburst winds causing a semi-truck to flip on I-10. The overall environment was characterized by MLCAPE values of around 1000 J/KG as well as DCAPE values well in excess of 1500 J/KG, which were favorable parameters to get severe downburst winds.
episodes.194577: An upper-level low triggered thunderstorms across the eastern mountains of Oregon during the afternoon and evening hours of July 24. Severe hail and damaging wind gusts were reported from the public in Grant, Union, and Wallowa Counties.
episodes.194629: Strong thunderstorms moved across the marine area and produced gusty winds.
episodes.194743: Deep moisture streamed across the area ahead of an upper trough. Heavy rain occured in the afternoon during max diurnal heating.
episodes.194763: Afternoon and evening thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce strong marine wind gusts over the Nature Coast, and central to southwest areas near Clearwater and Venice.
episodes.194765: Evening thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce wind damage near Brooksville in Hernando County.
episodes.194766: Evening thunderstorms associated with the sea breeze produce strong marine wind gusts in the Tampa Bay area.
episodes.194812: Scattered thunderstorms developed along a stationary front in the Atlanta metro and towards Macon. Heavy rainfall was the main threat, however isolated wind damage and strong storms were able to develop through the afternoon along a line stretching from between Atlanta and Macon up through Athens.
episodes.194917: Slow-moving bands of locally training showers and thunderstorms produced extremely heavy rainfall rates and excessive totals across southern Natchitoches Parish on the morning of July 24th. The convection was associated with a weak mid-level shortwave perturbation and an associated low-level trough, while also interacting with a very moist and moderately unstable air mass that was pooling northward from the Gulf of Mexico. Precipitable water values over the region were deeply tropical in nature, with values of 2.25 to 2.5 inches, and this coupled with the level of instability and forcing promoted rainfall rates reaching 2 to 3 inches/hour with the stronger cells. Cell training with these slow-moving linearly oriented bands of convection resulted in isolated flash flooding over parts of southern Natchitoches Parish.
episodes.194939: A frontal boundary supported scattered thunderstorms across Central New York. Ahead of the front, an unstable environment triggered rounds of repeating, heavy rain producing thunderstorms that moved over the same areas. Rainfall totals of 2-3 inches fell in less than 3 hours which contributed to localized flash and urban flooding.
episodes.194974: Monsoon moisture advecting around the periphery of the big ridge causing excessive heat fueled scattered thunderstorms. Several storms produced high winds and/or flooding.
episodes.194982: An wetter system moving through western Washington through the end of July brought some plentiful rainfall that broke some local records across the region.
episodes.195022: Hot and humid air mass produced diurnal convection that resulted in localized flash flooding at the University of Tennessee.
episodes.195050: A few diurnal thunderstorms developed along a surface boundary from southwest Minnesota into northwest Iowa, which had been reinforced by earlier day convection. The strongest storm along the line produced hail up to penny size.
episodes.195072: A frontal boundary initiated a line of thunderstorms across south-central Louisiana. This line was mostly decaying by the time it got to southeast Louisiana, but it was able to produce a strong wind gust across Lake Pontchartrain before it fully dissipated.
episodes.195152: A moist and unstable air mass was in place with dew points generally in the mid to upper 70s on July 24, 2024. This resulted in scattered heavy rain and flooding across portions of Central Virginia.
episodes.195154: A moist and unstable air mass was in place with dew points generally in the mid to upper 70s on July 24, 2024. This resulted in scattered heavy rain and flooding across portions of Central and Eastern Virginia as well as isolated severe storms across south central Virginia.
episodes.195218: A moist and unstable air mass was in place with dew points generally in the mid to upper 70s on July 23 and 24, 2024. This resulted in scattered heavy rain and flooding across portions of Central and Eastern Virginia.
episodes.195242: Kettle Butte measured a 63 mph wind gust.
episodes.195257: Several wildfires erupted in July, mainly late in the month. Hawarden fire in City of Riverside did the most damage.  The excessive heat caused rapid drying of the vegetation and fuels.
episodes.195993: At the surface, a cold front drifted southeastward from the Upper MS River Valley to far-southwestern ON, far-western Lake Erie, and northwest OH between the early afternoon of the 23rd and late morning of the 24th as a low moved east-northeastward from central Lake Michigan to Georgian Bay. The cold front then advanced farther southeastward to eastern Lake Erie, northwest PA, and northeast OH by the early evening of the 24th as the low moved northeastward to southwestern QC. This cold front encountered a warm and humid sector along the northwestern flank of the Bermuda-Azores subtropical high pressure ridge. Along and ahead of the cold front, several rounds of multicell thunderstorms impacted northeast OH and generated damaging straight-line convective wind gusts. These storms occurred in an environment comprised of moderate effective bulk shear, MUCAPE, and DCAPE, respectively.
episodes.195995: At the surface, a low moved northeastward from Georgian Bay to southwestern QC during the late morning through early evening of the 24th. Simultaneously, the trailing cold front swept southeastward from far-southwestern ON, far-western Lake Erie, and northwest OH to eastern Lake Erie, northwest PA, and northeast OH. This front encountered a warm and humid sector along the northwestern flank of the Bermuda-Azores subtropical high pressure ridge.  Ahead of the front, a cluster of multicell thunderstorms impacted the Erie metro area and generated isolated, damaging straight-line convective wind gusts. These storms occurred in an environment comprised of moderate effective bulk shear, MUCAPE, and DCAPE, respectively.
episodes.195996: At the surface, a low moved northeastward from Georgian Bay to central QC during the late morning of the 24th through late morning of the 25th. Simultaneously, the trailing cold front swept eastward and southeastward from far-southwestern ON, far-western Lake Erie, and northwest OH to northwestern New England, southeastern NY, northeastern and southwestern PA, and the Mid OH River Valley. Behind the cold front, a trough axis moved generally southward across Lake Erie during the morning hours of the 25th. ||Ahead of the cold front, a cluster of multicell thunderstorms generated gale-force peak convective wind gusts along the Cleveland lakeshore as the storms encountered moderate effective bulk shear, MUCAPE, and DCAPE, respectively, during the afternoon of the 24th. Behind the cold front, isolated multicell thunderstorms impacted western Lake Erie during the morning of the 25th as the aforementioned surface trough axis encountered weak to moderate MUCAPE and moderate effective bulk shear. The relatively-strong updraft of one of these storms managed to spawn a non-mesocyclonic waterspout near Cedar Point.

A weak EF0 tornado occurred on Wednesday, July 24, 2024 just east of Broadalbin, NY. The tornado touched down in the backyard of Cerrero's Cuts, before traveling across Route 29 and impacting a private residence on the north side of the highway. At this location, a few tree limbs were downed in the front yard, with two uprooted trees noted behind the residence. The convergent nature of the downed trees is consistent with a weak tornadic circulation. The tornado continued to the north before dissipating beyond the private residence property boundary. The park length was 0.16 miles with a path width of 30 yards.
